title: Exact module gluing across a finite clopen cover for arbitrary ring sheaves
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $I$ be a finite set, and let $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$ be pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes whose images cover $X$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use the small pro-etale sites and their fixed universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].

For any sheaf of commutative rings $R$ on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, put $R_i=R|_{X_i}$. In the abelian module-sheaf categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], restriction $r=(r_i)_i$ is an additive exact equivalence
$$\operatorname{Mod}(R)\simeq\prod_i\operatorname{Mod}(R_i).$$
An additive exact quasi-inverse is $G((F_i)_i)(U)=\prod_iF_i(U\times_X X_i)$ with componentwise restrictions and the $R(U)$-actions induced by restriction. The unit $F\to G(rF)$ is restriction of sections to the component cover of $U$, and the counit $r_iG(F_j)\to F_i$ is projection onto the $i$th factor. Both are natural isomorphisms. If $e_i$ is $G$ applied to the tuple with $F_i$ in coordinate $i$ and zero elsewhere, then $r_ie_i\cong1$, $r_ie_j=0$ for $i\ne j$, and $\bigoplus_i e_ir_i\cong1$. Kernels, cokernels and exact sequences are detected componentwise.

For the constant coefficient sheaves and completed integral sheaves of [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], the identifications $r_i(A_{E,n})_X\cong(A_{E,n})_{X_i}$ and $r_i\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}\cong\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X_i}$ preserve the constant sections, the projections to every finite quotient, and their transition maps. Here $\ell$ is a prime invertible on $X$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite, and $n\ge1$.

Empty components contribute zero module categories. If $I=\varnothing$, then $X=\varnothing$, and its module category is equivalent to the category with one object and one arrow.

source.place: Tag 04TS, sites-lemma-mapping-property-glue; Tags 04TQ/04TR, sites-lemma-glue-maps/sites-lemma-glue-sheaves. Agent finite-clopen module expansion of the section-invariant argument, old item steps 1-3.

proof.text: Use the actual composition and base-change functors of the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with module restriction as in [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. The proved source lemmas AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt.isContinuous_overMap, isCocontinuous_overMap and isContinuous_overPullback give their continuity properties. Base change the jointly surjective component family to each test object. The component inclusions are etale [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], so the resulting family is a pro-etale covering [lem-pur-etale-proetale-cover]. On distinct components every object mapping into both is empty, since its structural map has image in two disjoint subsets. The diagonal composition/base-change unit is an isomorphism: its inverse is the first pullback projection, since an open immersion is mono.

source.place: Definition 098K, definition-big-small-proetale; localization as in Definition 09AE, definition-extension-zero; agent finite-clopen specialization

proof.text: The empty family covers an empty object of the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. The proved source theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt.isTerminalSectionsOfIsEmpty makes the sections of any module sheaf a terminal abelian group. Such a group is zero, so these sections are subsingleton [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Matching conditions for sections over distinct components are therefore automatic.

source.place: Tag 04TR, lemma-glue-sheaves: gluing datum preceding the lemma; empty-overlap specialization

proof.text: Define $G(F_i)(U)=\prod_i F_i(U_i)$ as an abelian group, with $a(x_i)_i=(a|_{U_i}x_i)_i$ for $a\in R(U)$. For $v:V\to U$ restrict the $i$th coordinate along $V\times_X X_i\to U\times_X X_i$. The module laws and semilinearity hold in each coordinate by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so this is a presheaf of $R$-modules. For a tuple of module morphisms $(f_i)_i$ set $G(f_i)_U=\prod_i(f_i)_{U_i}$. The coordinate identities show functoriality and additivity. Restriction $r$ is also additive, since it evaluates the same morphisms on a smaller collection of objects.

source.place: Tag 04TR, lemma-glue-sheaves: compatible-tuples formula; componentwise module operations

proof.text: For each i, the base-change functor X_proet to (X_i)_proet is continuous. Pushforward of F_i along this functor, with the ring map R to the pushforward of R_i induced by the composition/base-change counit, is therefore an actual R-module sheaf. Define G as the explicit product presheaf of these sheaves. Its maps, actions and object data are componentwise constructions, not chosen witnesses. The concrete module products are limiting at every object, hence form a limit of module presheaves. Limits of sheaves are sheaves, so this same explicit presheaf is a module sheaf. This proves sheafness directly and does not use general effective descent [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Tag 03DB, limits of module sheaves; Mathlib PresheafOfModules.isSheaf_of_isLimit and continuous module pushforward; direct product construction replacing general descent

proof.text: For $F\in\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ let $\eta_F(U):F(U)\to G(rF)(U)$ be $(x|_{U_i})_i$. The same disjoint-cover sheaf axiom gives a bijection, and the component restrictions make it linear; hence $\eta_F$ is an isomorphism. For an object $W\to X_i$, $W\times_X X_i\cong W$ and $W\times_X X_j=\varnothing$ for $j\ne i$. Projection gives $\epsilon_i(W):r_iG(F_j)(W)\to F_i(W)$ with inverse $x\mapsto(0,\ldots,x,\ldots,0)$. It is a linear isomorphism, using the zero values in step 2. Both comparisons commute with restrictions and module morphisms by their formulas. After applying $r_i$, $\epsilon_i\circ r_i\eta$ sends $x$ to $x$. The other triangle sends a tuple $(x_i)_i$ to itself in every coordinate. Thus $r,G,\eta,\epsilon$ give the asserted additive equivalence.

source.place: Tags 04TQ and 04TS, lemma-glue-maps and lemma-mapping-property-glue; explicit finite-disjoint unit and counit

proof.text: Define $e_iM$ by applying $G$ to $M$ in coordinate $i$ and zero elsewhere. The counit formula gives $r_ie_iM\cong M$; for $k\ne i$ the same formula gives $r_ke_iM=0$ (canonically the zero module sheaf). There are inclusion maps $e_ir_iF\to F$: under $\eta_F$ they send a section in coordinate $i$ to the tuple with all other entries zero. Their sum gives $\bigoplus_i e_ir_iF\to F$. Its inverse sends $x\in F(U)$ to the finite sum of the inclusions of $x|_{U_i}$ into that direct sum. The two composites are identities coordinatewise, because a finite tuple is the sum of its coordinate tuples. These formulas also prove naturality and the direct-sum universal property (a map out is uniquely the sum of the component maps).

source.place: Tag 04TS, lemma-mapping-property-glue; agent finite-coordinate additive calculation

proof.text: By [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] all the module categories in question are abelian. In their product the tuple of kernels is a kernel and the tuple of cokernels is a cokernel: the factorization through each component is unique, hence the tuple factorization is unique. By [lem-galois-equivalence-preserves-limits], both functors of the equivalence preserve limits and colimits, in particular kernels and cokernels, so both are exact. This also proves detection, including the universal-property meaning: a proposed kernel or cokernel cone is universal precisely when its image under the equivalence is, since the inverse transports the factorization and its uniqueness back. The homology object $\ker(g)/\operatorname{im}(f)$ of a complex $F\xrightarrow f H\xrightarrow g K$ is therefore zero precisely when all its component homology objects are zero. This is exactly componentwise detection of exact sequences. No sectionwise surjectivity assertion about a sheaf epimorphism is used.

source.place: Tag 03DB, lemma-limits-colimits; categorical preservation of limits and colimits by equivalences (Categories Tag 0038)

proof.text: For a constant commutative ring A, use the inverse of the sheafification compatibility isomorphism for the continuous and cocontinuous composition functor on the small pro-etale sites. After forgetting to rings this gives r_i(A_X) isomorphic to A_(X_i). The compatibility identity with the sheafification unit proves preservation of constant sections. Naturality of the sheafification compatibility proves naturality in every ring homomorphism A to B. Apply this to the finite quotient rings and their transition homomorphisms [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. No full localized-site equivalence is used.

source.place: Localization Section 00XZ; constant-ring localization as in clause (2) of the cited node

proof.text:
By [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] the completed ring is $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}=\varprojlim_n(A_{E,n})_X$. By the ring clause of [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit] this limit is evaluated sectionwise. Thus for $W\to X_i$, restriction and step 8 give the ring isomorphism
$$
 (r_i\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X})(W)=\varprojlim_n (A_{E,n})_X(W)\ \cong\ \varprojlim_n(A_{E,n})_{X_i}(W)=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X_i}(W).
$$
It sends a compatible tuple $(a_n)_n$ to the tuple obtained by applying the finite-level comparison to each $a_n$. Step 8 ensures compatibility with the transitions, and taking the $n$th coordinate is exactly the comparison with the projection $\pi_n$. A constant $a\in\mathcal O_E$ corresponds to its compatible residues, each of which is preserved in step 8, so these constant sections are preserved too. The formulas commute with restrictions in $W$. This proves the completed identification with all the required normalizations; it does not replace the completed sheaf by the discrete constant $\mathcal O_E$-sheaf.

source.place: Tags 03CO (2) and 03DB, lemma-limits-colimits-abelian-sheaves and lemma-limits-colimits; coordinatewise ring limit

proof.text: If $X_i=\varnothing$, every object over it is empty and step 2 makes every module sheaf zero, with exactly one morphism between any two such sheaves. Such a factor is therefore equivalent to the one-object, one-arrow category and has no effect on the equivalence. If $I=\varnothing$, the covering assumption forces $X=\varnothing$; the product defining $G$ is the one-element abelian group, with its unique module structure. Step 2 then says that every module sheaf on $X$ is uniquely isomorphic to it and all morphisms are unique. This verifies the asserted empty-index equivalence as well as all the zero-factor conventions.
